title: Curriculum Design for Continuing Professional Education Across Forensic Disciplines: A Scoping Review Protocol
content: Introduction: Continuing professional education in forensic practice requires curricula that address disciplinary expertise, interpretation, documentation, and communication while remaining responsive to changing professional needs. This scoping review aims to map how continuing professional education curricula are designed, delivered, assessed, evaluated, and quality-assured across forensic disciplines, including their relationship to ongoing professional competence. Accreditation, certification, and governance will be examined in relation to how they shape educational arrangements. Methods: The review will follow Arksey and O’Malley’s five-stage framework, incorporating Levac and colleagues’ refinements and JBI guidance. Reporting will follow PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, and APA PsycINFO will be searched from inception to the final search date, with reference-list searching providing additional sources. Inclusion will be restricted to English-language publications without geographical restrictions. Eligible sources will address continuing professional education or competence maintenance among qualified or practicing forensic professionals and provide substantive information on curriculum design or educational assurance. Sources concerning only undergraduate, pre-licensure, entry-to-practice, or initial specialist education will be excluded unless a separable continuing-development component is reported. Two reviewers will independently screen titles, abstracts, and full texts using Covidence, with disagreements resolved through discussion or a third reviewer. A standardized charting form will be piloted on at least five eligible sources; one reviewer will chart each source, and a second will verify all entries. Results and Analysis: Data will be summarized descriptively and synthesized narratively across the following: learning needs assessment; competencies and objectives; curriculum content and structure; teaching and implementation; assessment and feedback; evaluation and revision; and educational quality assurance. Reported outcomes will be mapped to the four Kirkpatrick levels: reaction, learning, behavior, and results. Measurement methods and follow-up periods will be retained to distinguish immediate learning outcomes from retained competence and workplace application. The synthesis will identify shared educational elements, disciplinary variations, accessibility barriers, and reporting or evaluation gaps to inform subsequent curriculum development. Ethics and Dissemination: Ethical approval is not anticipated because the review will analyze published literature without collecting identifiable participant data. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, relevant professional meetings, and curriculum design summaries for educators, practitioners, professional associations, accrediting organizations, and forensic service leaders.
